chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dehqan, from Durost ibn Abi Mansoor, from Abdullah ibn Sin'an, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:
Do not use the stem of sweet basil or the twig of the pomegranate tree as toothpicks, for they stir up the sweat of leprosy.
ai.seo_question: Why should one avoid using basil or pomegranate twigs as toothpicks according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) within the context of practical hygiene and medical wisdom, linking specific botanical properties to the aggravation of leprosy (*Jadham*) through the stimulation of bodily humors. This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of integrating prophetic medical advice with observable physiological effects, emphasizing preventive care in daily rituals.
